slot.brief: An atom (hydrogen-like) absorbs a photon of given energy; identify which transitions are possible from the ground state and find the level reached or the number of possible emission lines in the resulting de-excitation cascade.

stem: A hydrogen-like ion has ground-state ionization energy $54.4\ \text{eV}$. Starting in its ground state, it absorbs a $51.0\ \text{eV}$ photon. Find the principal quantum number reached and the maximum number of distinct emission lines possible in its subsequent de-excitation.

verdicts.working: Use $54.4(1-1/n^2)=51.0$, giving $1/n^2=1/16$ and $n=4$. The maximum number of distinct lines is $4(4-1)/2=6$.

working:
$54.4\left(1-\dfrac{1}{n^2}\right)=51.0\Rightarrow n=4$; $N=\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}=\dfrac{4\cdot3}{2}=6$.

Independent check: Use $54.4(1-1/n^2)=51.0$, giving $1/n^2=1/16$ and $n=4$. The maximum number of distinct lines is $4(4-1)/2=6$.
solution:
For absorption from the ground state, $54.4\left(1-\dfrac{1}{n^2}\right)=51.0$, giving $n=4$. The maximum number of distinct emission lines is
$$N=\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}=\dfrac{4\cdot3}{2}=6.$$
